title: Positional parameter misalignment in tool/function calling when payloads include BOM/CRLF and nulls
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Customer reports: Several customers observed that when invoking function/tool calls that rely on positional (ordered) parameters, values become misaligned after a function response contains certain byte sequences (UTF-8 BOM), CRLF line endings, or explicit null values in the top-level array/object. The downstream mapping layer maps shifted indexes to the wrong argument names, causing incorrect behavior in the customer's service. Impact spans Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (on-prem proxy) deployments but is most common in Private with older TLS offload/proxy stacks.
acceptance_criteria: Parser no longer shifts positional args when BOM or leading CRLF present in response payload
Structured output validator rejects ambiguous toolcall payloads and returns a deterministic error for callers
E2E repro from customer payloads passes in hosted, dedicated, and private test clusters
Canary rollout (10% traffic) shows zero new misaligned mappings and no regression in latency under CI workload
steps_to_reproduce:
Use the customer's sample: function returns JSON array with a leading UTF-8 BOM (﻿) followed by CRLF and then valid JSON: e.g., "﻿
[null, "valueA", 42]"
Call Redwood API with function signature that expects positional params: (user_id, action, count)
Observe mapping: parser binds user_id -> null, action -> "valueA", count -> 42 OR in some deployments binds user_id -> "valueA" (index shift), depending on proxy behavior
Repeat the same payload through Private deployment behind nginx TLS offload with chunked transfer and compare results
investigation_notes: 02/14 - Triage: Customer provided 3 request traces (hosted, dedicated, private). All traces show identical token payloads but different parser outcomes in Private cluster

02/15 - Repro: Local integration tests reproduced misalignment when payload contained BOM followed by CRLF. Jackson-based parser path used in dedicated/private runtime did not strip BOM before token alignment. Hosted runtime had an upstream normalizer that removed BOMs, explaining environment discrepancy

02/17 - Deeper: The streaming adapter that performs chunk reassembly can emit an empty token when BOM+CRLF are present and when upstream proxy performs chunk boundary splits at those bytes. The positional-argument indexer uses token emission counts to assign indexes — empty emission yields shift
02/18 - Edgecases: Null values in top-level arrays combined with BOM/CRLF sometimes co-occur with proxies that insert or drop a CR; this further changes array offsets after streaming reassembly
02/20 - Customer impact: Medium-high for customers using positional tool calls; some production mappings resulted in accidental data writes. No PII exfiltration seen in logs but behavior is unsafe

02/24 - Hypothesis: Fix options are (A) normalize/strip BOM and leading CR/LF at the streaming adapter boundary, (B) change indexer to use structural parsing (bracket-aware) instead of token counts, (C) add strict schema enforcement that rejects non-conforming payloads with clear error messages

02/25 - Decision: Implement combination of (A) and (B): strip control bytes early + make indexer robust to empty emissions by buffering until a structural start token is observed. Add schema validation as fallback (C) for maximum safety

02/26 - Found regression in an internal compatibility test with legacy private runtime (1.18): new stripping logic caused small latency increase under synthetic microbenchmarks (~0.4ms median). We will gate the change with canary and optimize after rollout
actions: Create PR with streaming-adapter BOM/CRLF stripper and unit tests (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1538)
Refactor positional indexer to buffer until structural tokens '[' or '{' are seen and skip empty emissions
Add integration tests that simulate chunked boundary splits at BOM/CRLF and null values
Deploy to dedicated-canary cluster (10% traffic) and private test harness used by SE before broader rollout
Notify affected customers with remediation steps and ETA; provide workaround to switch to named-parameter calls until fix is deployed
blocked_by: ENG-31209 (tenant-kvcache-session-tagging-fix) - needs slight runtime I/O change merged first
notes_for_reviews: Code change must preserve existing performance for hosted path (there is an upstream normalizer); add opt-in config to disable BOM stripping in weird legacy environments
QA should validate both named and positional tool calls, with and without BOM/CRLF, and run across OS-level lineending differences
Security: confirm no new logging of full customer payloads in production; any temporary logs should be redacted
